newsitem.title: USA: Salomon stays overweight in Mexico,Brazil equities.
newsitem.headline: Salomon stays overweight in Mexico,Brazil equities.

text.p: A Salomon Brothers strategist said Friday he recommended keeping overweight positions for Mexico and Brazil in a model Latin American stock portfolio.
John Mullin, Salomon's Latin American equity strategist, said in a report the region's strong bull market was likely to remain intact through August despite a dip this month.
Over the longer term, he wrote, "We believe that there is still some room for multiple expansion in Latin America, albeit not as much room as existed several months ago."
His recommendations on portfolio allocations were:
-- Overweight Mexico, "the most attractive value play of the large Latin American markets. Despite the market's 39 percent increase this year, its valuation multiples remain relatively inexpensive."
-- Overweight Brazil. The Sao Paulo exchange's recent drop sparked in part by worries about a currency devaluation is "an excellent buying opportunity.
"... We believe that a substantial exchange rate devaluation is highly unlikely this year."
-- Underweight Argentina. "Much good news has been built into the valuations of Argentine cyclicals, including steel, cement and banking.
"In our view, these expensive valuations cap the upside for the Argentine market."

-- Underweight Chile, because of expensive valuations, good economic news already built into prices, lack of demand for equities from local pension funds and the prospect of disappointing second-quarter earnings.
Of other Latin American markets, Colombia and Venezuela stayed overweight and Peru remained underweight.
The neutral weighting is based on a company capitalization-weighted benchmark consisting of 220 companies.
